title: The Llama 4 Herd: Natively Multimodal, Mixture-of-Experts
hook: Llama 4 is Meta's first mixture-of-experts family - only 17B parameters fire per token, but the full models hold hundreds of billions, and they read text, images, and video natively.
key_points: Meta's first MoE Llama family, and natively multimodal via early fusion of text, image, and video rather than a bolted-on vision adapter.
Llama 4 Scout: 17B active params, 16 experts, 109B total, with a 10M-token context window.
Llama 4 Maverick: 17B active params, 128 experts, 400B total.
Llama 4 Behemoth: a preview only, still training, at 288B active params and roughly 2T total.
Scout and Maverick are open-weight, downloadable day-one from llama.com and Hugging Face.
content_html: Meta released the Llama 4 herd in April 2025, its first mixture-of-experts language model family and the first built to be natively multimodal. Two models ship open-weight on day one - Llama 4 Scout and Llama 4 Maverick - while a much larger model, Behemoth, was shown only as a preview while still training.
extra_html:
What's new

Where earlier Llama models were dense - every parameter runs on every token - Llama 4 uses mixture-of-experts, so only a fraction of the network activates per token. Scout runs 17B active parameters across 16 experts (109B total) and carries a 10M-token context window; Maverick keeps the same 17B active but spreads them across 128 experts for 400B total. Multimodality comes from early fusion: text, image, and video are combined into the model's input rather than handled by a separate add-on. Behemoth, previewed but unreleased, runs 288B active parameters out of roughly 2T total.

Why it matters

MoE lets Meta grow total capacity into the hundreds of billions of parameters while keeping the per-token compute close to a 17B model, and early-fusion multimodality means images and video are first-class inputs rather than an afterthought. Scout and Maverick being open-weight day-one on llama.com and Hugging Face keeps the most capable open ecosystem moving. See Meta's announcement for full details.

related.title: The Llama 3 Herd of Models
related.hook: Meta's Llama 3 family, trained on roughly 15 trillion tokens with a 405B-parameter flagship, narrowed the gap to closed frontier models while staying open-weights.

related.title: Mixtral of Experts
related.hook: Mixtral packs 8 experts per layer but routes each token through only 2, so you get the capacity of a ~47B model at the compute cost of a ~13B one - open weights included.

related.title: What Is a Mixture of Experts?
related.hook: Instead of running every input through one big network, route each token to a few specialist sub-networks - total capacity grows without proportional compute.

related.title: Muse Glimmer: Meta's 30B Local Agentic Multimodal Model
related.hook: Meta distilled its Muse model down to 30B and shipped it Apache 2.0 — a vision-and-text model built to run locally and call tools, not just chat.
